# First Transatlantic Phone Call 

The first public test of radio-telephone service from New York to London was made in 1926. The commercial transatlantic telephone service began on January 7, 1927 with a call between Walter S Gifford, the president of AT&T, in NY, and Sir Evelyn Murray, the Secretary of the General Post Office. Following their call, the commercial service was opened to the public. Being based on radio, the service was affected by atmospheric interference, which wasn't solved until the installation of the TAT-1 trans-Atlantic cable in 1956.
